title: Autonomous VPC networking scaffolder with canary route upgrades and health-driven rollbacks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: deliver a composable Terraform module (vpc_scaffolder) that provisions subnets (public/private), NAT (NAT Gateway + optional NAT instances), IGW, VPC endpoints (S3, DynamoDB, ECR, SecretsManager, STS), route tables, and automated canary-friendly route upgrades with health-driven rollback hooks. The module should be opinionated about safe defaults but extensible for customer overrides (subnet sizing, multi-AZ placement, endpoint selection, egress policies). It must include:
- A versioned module API with clear upgrade notes and migration helpers for state changes.
- A built-in synthetic egress probing system (Lambda or container) to run active connectivity checks for each AZ/subnet after provisioning or route changes.
- Canary route rollout primitives: ability to shift a percentage of egress via alternate NATs/paths and run healthbeat checks, then commit or rollback changes automatically.
- Drift detection hooks integrated with CI (tf plan -> diff sanitizer -> optional auto-apply) and a state snapshot/backup step before upgrades.
- Policy guardrail checks (OPA/Preflight) for disallowed public routes and missing endpoints for sensitive services.
- Outputs and meta-attributes consumed by our Private control plane (VPC id, route-table ids, endpoint ids, healthcheck stream ARNs).
Why this is different: instead of a plain VPC module, this scaffolder is oriented around safe upgrades and operational readiness for Private deployments where upgrades must not cause customer-visible outages. It ties terraform lifecycle actions to short-lived runtime probes and CI gating so infra changes can be validated automatically before being promoted to production environments.
acceptance_criteria: Module instantiates a default multi-AZ VPC with public and private subnets and returns standardized outputs
Canary route change can be executed (10% -> 50% -> 100%) via module parameters or a TF plan step and the system runs probes for each stage
If probes detect degradation beyond threshold (packet loss or request latency), the module's upgrade hook triggers an automated rollback and leaves prior routes intact
Terraform plan/upgrade process includes a pre-upgrade snapshot step and generates a human-readable upgrade summary in CI
OPA/Preflight policies block changes that would remove required VPC endpoints for regulated customers
Module includes documented migration steps for renaming route table resources and changing subnet CIDAM layout without data loss
Integration test harness (local) reproduces a canary rollout and rollback using mocked egress targets

risks: Automated rollback could trigger frequent flips under noisy probe thresholds — need conservative defaults and jittered sampling
Stateful renames (route tables, nat attachments) risk losing references in customer terraform stacks — include migration helper script
Prober Lambda cold-starts could skew early-stage canary metrics — mitigate by warmers or short warm-up stage
OPA policy false-positives may block legitimate upgrades for customers with custom egress patterns — include policy override path for support-tickets
implementation_notes: Technical approach: create a core module 'vpc_scaffolder' that composes smaller submodules (subnet, nat, endpoints, route-table). Each resource set exposes a 'health_probe_target' output used by the canary-orchestrator. Upgrade flow: 1) CI kicks off 'tf plan' -> 2) snapshot current state to S3 with timestamped key -> 3) apply canary changes (using route weighting tags and target groups) -> 4) trigger prober runs for N minutes -> 5a) if pass -> apply remaining changes and tag release; 5b) if fail -> automatically re-apply snapshot or restore prior route associations and create incident ticket. Implementation detail: we will avoid provider-specific tricks; use AWS native constructs (RouteTable, NatGateway, AWS::EC2::ClientVpnEndpoint not required). For customers with strict compliance, module exposes 'skip_autorollback' flag and an audit hook that posts the before/after plan to a secure S3 bucket. Use semantic module versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) and include an 'upgrade_notes' file in the module registry. Testing: unit tests with Terratest, integration harness in ephemeral AWS accounts, and local acceptance flow with localstack for fast iteration.
